result.title: When Sparsity Breaks Connectivity: Functional Reachability and Guided Topology Dynamics in Extreme Sparse Training
result.summary: Dynamic Sparse Training (DST) periodically prunes and regrows connections, inducing a discrete dynamical mechanism over network topologies. At extreme sparsity ($\ge 99\%$), this dynamic tends to destroy input-output information pathways, and performance with standard magnitude/random updates degrades sharply. We formalize forward, backward, and functional reachability on layered sparse graphs, derive closed-form expectations for reachable neurons and edges, and show that Monte Carlo realizations match the theory. Guided by this reachability-based structure, we bias pruning toward non-functional edges and regrowth toward functionally consistent candidates. We introduce this reachability-driven modification of topology evolution as Reachability-guided in DST, referred to as guided DST. On CIFAR-10/100 and Tiny ImageNet, guided DST recovers large accuracy gaps versus unguided DST (up to $+14.4$ points at $99.9\%$ sparsity on CIFAR-100), and on MLP-Mixer guided DST remains trainable at $99.99\%$ sparsity while unguided random regrowth degrades sharply. These results cast extreme-sparse training as a connectivity-preserving dynamical process. Our implementation is publicly available at https://github.com/mzjaworski/ea_dst.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究极端稀疏（≥99%）下动态稀疏训练的拓扑演化，形式化前向、反向与功能可达性并给出闭式期望，据此引导剪枝与再生长以保住输入-输出通路，在 CIFAR 与 Tiny ImageNet 上显著缩小与随机更新的差距。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「功能可达性」把通路是否存在而非参数多少作为判断依据，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据通路被切断、信息坍缩的度量与干预提供类比线索；但图结构假设与 latent 状态更新的可比性尚待核查。
